intended_object: This is an auxiliary proposition for the library's Grushko/Stallings-folding proof of Marshall Hall's theorem. The docstring calls it "a graph-level formulation of the one point still missing from the fold argument": every generating, weakly connected, reverse-free marked graph that satisfies the Euler bound and has more than one vertex has a null path from the base vertex whose first edge can be folded safely.
explanation: `HasSafeNullFold` is not a standard mathematical object. It is a hypothesis invented for this proof: it isolates the step of the fold argument that the library has not yet proved. The global termination induction in this file takes it as its only assumption, and `hasSafeNullFold_of_hasGeometricallySimpleNullPath` derives it from a weaker-looking auxiliary hypothesis. Its ingredients are all internal to the library: `MarkedBinaryGraph`, `foldSymmPathAvoid`, `symmOrientedArrow`, and the particular Euler bound `card AllArrow ≤ 2(n + |V| - 1)`. The literature has no notion of a "safe null fold" property to compare it against. It is a proof device, so it has no Mathlib counterpart.
